question: Should Linux `system.notify` be implemented in the core headless node host now, and if so which backend/dependency contract should OpenClaw support first?
rationale: The exact command is reserved by core and cannot be filled by a plugin, but backend choice affects dependency expectations, headless behavior, and safe process invocation.

options.title: Core notify-send first
options.body: Implement a narrow core node-host handler that uses `notify-send` when a desktop session is present, returns structured unavailable results otherwise, and documents any optional OS package dependency.

options.title: Broader desktop backend matrix
options.body: Design a larger backend layer that includes D-Bus and/or `dunstify`, accepting extra implementation and support scope before work starts.

options.title: Defer to Linux companion app
options.body: Keep headless node-host notifications unsupported and let the broader Linux companion app direction own desktop notification delivery later.

recommendation.title: Core notify-send first
recommendation.body: Implement a narrow core node-host handler that uses `notify-send` when a desktop session is present, returns structured unavailable results otherwise, and documents any optional OS package dependency.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest feature-history and product-direction signal for the node notification surface and Linux companion direction.
